title: Quantifying the Lithiation Heterogeneities in Aged Thick Gr-Si Electrodes for Battery Applications
content: Batteries, and Li-ion batteries, are a key focus point for research around sustainable development due to the stakes of energy storage in portable devices and the current shift of the automotive industry away from combustion engines towards hybrid or full electric vehicles (EV). From the EV standpoint, batteries should have a high energy density (drive longer) and high power density (good acceleration and fast charging). Highly loaded Gr/Si composite electrodes are good candidates to meet these expectations as negative electrodes with high theoretical energy density. However, Si particles undergo a huge morphology change during cycling (particle swelling, pulverization), changing the local electrode structure in a non-negligible manner and leading to irreversible capacity loss [1 - 4].
